summary: Targi is a tight, elegant two-player worker-placement game where you and your opponent each place four meeples around a shared 5x5 grid, with placement restrictions forcing you to react to your opponent's choices turn by turn. Most of the tension comes from figuring out which resource/action combo lets you snag the tribe cards you need while denying your opponent theirs.
praised: Extremely tight, elegant design with almost no wasted rules for a two-player-only game
Clever placement restriction (can't sit on or directly across from an opponent's meeple) creates real tactical tension
Fast to teach and plays quickly once learned
High replayability from the shifting mix of tribe cards and market cards each game
criticised: Can feel solved or samey after many plays since the board and core actions never change
Some randomness in which tribe/market cards appear can swing available strategies
Rulebook/first-play icon overload makes the opening learning curve steeper than the game actually is

interaction.kind: blocking and area denial via meeple placement

scoring.why: Points come from a mix of tribe card sets, gold, and end-game bonuses, so the winner is decided by who best converts limited worker placements into the right combination of cards and resources

similar: Agricola: All Creatures Big and Small
